title: Data Representation (Binary, Hex & Character Sets)
reason: No mark-affecting contradictions were found; referring to ASCII using 7 or 8 bits reflects standard discussion of 7-bit ASCII stored in an 8-bit byte.

pedantry.video_says: Because it only uses 7 or 8 bits for each character, it has a limit of 128 boxes.
pedantry.lesson_says: ASCII, which uses 7 bits per character and can therefore represent 128 different characters... 8 bits hold 2^8 = 256.
